Short commercial view: prioritize closing & revenue but avoid opening up unlimited downstream exposure. If Acme insists on mutual exclusion, request explicit carve-outs that preserve our indemnities and IP warranty remedies, and keep caps tied to the order form/fees (12 months' fees or fixed cap).

Suggested negotiation moves:
- Offer mutual exclusion but add explicit carve-outs: (a) willful misconduct; (b) breach of confidentiality; (c) indemnified claims (IP, data breach).
- Preserve a monetary cap tied to the OF (12 months' committed spend) instead of a global MSA-level change.
- If they reject, offer a compromise two-way-for-core and one-way-for-third-party-slow-floats (i.e., mutual for direct/consequential, but keep punitive/incidental carved out on their side).

If legal can draft a short paragraph tonight, I'll share it back to Claire with an ask to accept in the OF.

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the redline and Claire's note. High-level legal assessment: we can accept a mutual exclusion in the Order Form with controlled carve-outs, provided we keep a defined cap and explicit exclusions that preserve our core protections. The risk is manageable if the language is circumscribed to the Order Form and doesn't amend core MSA indemnities.

Proposed compromise language (short paragraph to include in the OF under "Limitation of Liability"):

"Except with respect to (i) Customer's breach of Section Confidentiality, (ii) indemnified claims arising from Customer's acts or data, (iii) Redwood's willful misconduct, and (iv) amounts payable under applicable law (including statutory fines), neither party shall be liable to the other for consequential, special, incidental, exemplary, indirect or punitive damages arising out of or related to this Order Form. Each party's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or relating to this Order Form shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Customer under this Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. The foregoing limitations shall not apply to (a) claims for indemnity, (b) breach of confidentiality obligations, or (c) damages resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence."

Notes on drafting and exposure:
- Cap tied to OF fees (12 months) keeps exposure bounded and is acceptable commercially.
- The carve-outs preserve indemnity and confidentiality, and keep punitive/willful outside the exclusion.
- Recommend we attach a redline snippet to the OF (see redline_exclusion_snippet.txt) and communicate that this is OF-level only — not a MSA amendment.

Operational ask: Ben/Aisha, if you want to present this, I can attach the snippet to an email to Claire and offer to sign the OF if they accept. If they push for broader MSA language, we should escalate to Legal Counsel (Karthik can take on escalation).

—Laura

Redwood Inference
